items.q: At the checkout, the ______ scanned my items and asked if I wanted a bag.
items.vi: Ở quầy tính tiền, nhân viên thu ngân quét các món hàng của tôi và hỏi tôi có cần túi không.
items.explanation: A cashier takes payment at the checkout. A customer is the buyer, an accountant keeps company accounts and a banker works in a bank.

items.q: Thousands of ______ cheered when the striker scored in the last minute.
items.vi: Hàng nghìn khán giả reo hò khi tiền đạo ghi bàn ở phút cuối.
items.explanation: Spectators are the people watching a sports event. Witnesses see a crime or accident, observers watch officially, and audience is a group noun that is not counted as 'thousands of audiences'.

items.q: My sister's ______ in the chess final was a boy who had never lost a game.
items.vi: Đối thủ của chị tôi trong trận chung kết cờ vua là một cậu bé chưa từng thua ván nào.
items.explanation: An opponent is the person you play against. A partner or teammate plays on your side, and a colleague works with you.

items.q: The ______ blew her whistle and told the children to get out of the pool.
items.vi: Nhân viên cứu hộ thổi còi và bảo bọn trẻ ra khỏi hồ bơi.
items.explanation: A lifeguard watches swimmers at a pool or beach. A bodyguard protects a person, a doorman stands at a building's entrance, and a guardian is legally responsible for a child.

items.q: A famous ______ with two million subscribers reviews new phones on her video channel every week.
items.vi: Một vlogger nổi tiếng với hai triệu người đăng ký đánh giá điện thoại mới trên kênh video của cô ấy mỗi tuần.
items.explanation: A vlogger makes videos for a channel. A blogger writes posts, an editor checks and corrects texts, and a reporter writes news.

items.q: Before buying the phone, Nam ______ a lot of research online.
items.vi: Trước khi mua điện thoại, Nam đã tìm hiểu rất nhiều trên mạng.
items.explanation: The collocation is do research; we do not say 'make', 'take' or 'give' research.

items.q: Choose a ______ password so that nobody can get into your account.
items.vi: Hãy chọn một mật khẩu mạnh để không ai vào được tài khoản của bạn.
items.explanation: A password that is difficult to guess is a strong password; 'heavy', 'hard' and 'powerful' do not collocate with 'password'.

items.q: Please ______ attention when the referee explains the rules of the game.
items.vi: Hãy chú ý khi trọng tài giải thích luật của trận đấu.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is pay attention; 'give', 'take' and 'make' are not used with 'attention' in this meaning.

items.q: Even though it started to rain, the players ______ with the match until the referee stopped it.
items.vi: Dù trời bắt đầu mưa, các cầu thủ vẫn tiếp tục trận đấu cho đến khi trọng tài dừng lại.
items.explanation: A finished past story told in order (it started to rain, they carried on, the referee stopped it) uses the past simple: carried on.

items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Nam's mum: He ______ football in the park at the moment.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu ạ? / Mẹ Nam: Nó đang đá bóng trong công viên.
items.explanation: At the moment signals an action happening now, so the present continuous is playing is needed.

items.q: I ______ this phone for three years, so it's time to buy a new one.
items.vi: Tôi đã dùng chiếc điện thoại này ba năm rồi, nên đã đến lúc mua cái mới.
items.explanation: A situation that began in the past and continues now, with for three years, takes the present perfect: have had.

items.q: By the time the shop opened, dozens of people ______ outside for hours.
items.vi: Đến lúc cửa hàng mở cửa, hàng chục người đã đứng chờ bên ngoài suốt mấy tiếng.
items.explanation: An activity that continued up to a past moment (by the time the shop opened) with for hours takes the past perfect continuous: had been waiting.

items.q: Lan: Do you know a shop called Phone World? / Nam: The name ______, but I can't remember where it is.
options: hits the nail on the head
items.vi: Lan: Cậu biết cửa hàng tên Phone World không? / Nam: Cái tên nghe quen quen, nhưng tớ không nhớ nó ở đâu.
items.explanation: Ring a bell means 'sound familiar'. Break the ice is to make people relax, hit the nail on the head is to be exactly right, and get on someone's nerves is to annoy them.

items.q: Our team played well in the first half but ______ after the break and lost 3-1.
items.vi: Đội chúng tôi chơi tốt ở hiệp một nhưng đuối sức sau giờ nghỉ và thua 3-1.
items.explanation: Run out of steam means to lose energy and stop trying hard. Hit the roof is to get very angry, miss the boat is to lose a chance, and make ends meet is to have just enough money.

items.q: The shop ______ my request for a refund because I had lost the receipt.
items.vi: Cửa hàng đã từ chối yêu cầu hoàn tiền của tôi vì tôi làm mất hóa đơn.
items.explanation: Turn down means to refuse a request or offer. Turn up is to arrive or increase, turn over is to flip something, and turn off is to switch off.

items.q: Please don't ______ the money I owe you in front of my parents.
items.vi: Làm ơn đừng nhắc đến số tiền tớ nợ cậu trước mặt bố mẹ tớ.
items.explanation: Bring up means to mention a subject. Bring back is to return something, bring about is to cause, and bring in is to introduce or earn.

items.q: Nam paid full price in the shop. He ______ have bought the phone online, where the same model is much cheaper.
items.vi: Nam đã trả nguyên giá ở cửa hàng. Lẽ ra cậu ấy nên mua điện thoại trên mạng, nơi cùng mẫu đó rẻ hơn nhiều.
items.explanation: Should have + past participle criticises a past action that was not done. Must have is a deduction, can't have a negative deduction, and needn't have means it was unnecessary but done.

items.q: Lan ______ have spent much money at the market - she only bought a keyring.
items.vi: Lan không thể nào tiêu nhiều tiền ở chợ được - cô ấy chỉ mua một cái móc khóa.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle says the speaker is sure something did NOT happen. Must have is a positive deduction, should have gives criticism, and needn't have means something was done unnecessarily.

items.q: The girl ______ phone was stolen on the bus reported it to the police.
items.vi: Cô gái có điện thoại bị lấy cắp trên xe buýt đã báo cảnh sát.
items.explanation: Whose shows possession (the girl's phone). Who and whom replace a person, and which replaces a thing, but none of them can stand before a noun like 'phone'.

items.q: The shop ______ I bought my headphones has closed down.
items.vi: Cửa hàng nơi tôi mua tai nghe đã đóng cửa rồi.
items.explanation: Where replaces 'in the shop' - a place with a full clause after it. Which or that would need a preposition ('from which'), and whose shows possession.

items.q: There isn't ______ time left before the sale ends, so hurry up.
items.vi: Không còn nhiều thời gian trước khi đợt giảm giá kết thúc, nên nhanh lên.
items.explanation: Time is uncountable, so a negative sentence takes much; many, a few and few go with plural countable nouns.

items.q: Don't forget ______ your phone before the match; you'll want to take photos.
items.vi: Đừng quên sạc điện thoại trước trận đấu; cậu sẽ muốn chụp ảnh đấy.
items.explanation: Forget to do refers to a task you need to do; forget doing means having no memory of something already done, and the bare form and 'to charging' are ungrammatical here.

items.q: The tickets were quite expensive; ______, the stadium was completely full.
items.vi: Vé khá đắt; tuy nhiên, sân vận động vẫn chật kín.
items.explanation: Two contrasting ideas joined with a semicolon and a comma need the adverb however. Therefore shows result, and because and although are conjunctions that cannot sit between a semicolon and a comma.

items.q: If I ______ so much on clothes last month, I could buy those trainers now.
items.vi: Nếu tháng trước tôi không tiêu quá nhiều vào quần áo thì bây giờ tôi đã có thể mua đôi giày thể thao đó.
items.explanation: A mixed conditional: an unreal past condition (last month) takes the past perfect hadn't spent, with a present result (could buy ... now).

items.q: Only after the final whistle ______ how tired he was.
items.vi: Chỉ sau tiếng còi kết thúc Nam mới nhận ra mình mệt đến thế nào.
items.explanation: After Only after ... at the start of a sentence, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: did Nam realise.
